recipe.title: Poulet rôti au citron et piment, riz pilaf aux carottes et tomates
recipe.description: Cuisses de poulet marinées au citron et piment, rôties au four, accompagnées d'un riz pilaf parfumé aux tomates, carottes et oignons.
instructions: Préchauffe le four à 200 °C.
Dans un bol, presse le jus d'1 citron, ajoute le zeste du deuxième citron, le piment finement haché, 2 gousses d'ail écrasées, 1 c. à soupe d'huile, du sel et du poivre ; mélange bien.
Enduis les 4 cuisses de poulet avec la marinade, puis place-les sur une plaque de cuisson recouverte de papier sulfurisé.
Enfourne et fais rôtir 35 minutes à feu moyen, jusqu'à ce que la peau soit dorée et que la température interne atteigne 74 °C (jus clair).
Pendant ce temps, rince le riz à l'eau froide puis égoutte.
Émince 1 oignon, coupe les 2 tomates en dés et les 2 carottes en rondelles fines.
Dans une casserole, fais chauffer 2 c. à soupe d'huile à feu moyen, ajoute l'oignon et fais-le dorer 3 minutes, jusqu'à ce qu'il devienne translucide.
Ajoute les dés de tomate et les rondelles de carotte, fais revenir 4 minutes, jusqu'à ce que les légumes commencent à ramollir.
Incorpore le riz, mélange 2 minutes pour enrober les grains d'huile et de légumes.
Verse 600 ml d'eau, porte à ébullition, puis couvre et laisse cuire à feu doux 15 minutes, jusqu'à absorption complète de l'eau et riz tendre.
Vérifie l'assaisonnement, ajoute une pincée de sel si besoin, puis sers le poulet rôti sur le lit de riz pilaf.
tips: Pour une peau encore plus croustillante, passe le poulet sous le gril 2 minutes à la fin de la cuisson.

recipe.title: Soupe épicée de poulet à la sauce d'arachide et riz
recipe.description: Une soupe onctueuse à base de bouillon de poulet, enrichie de pâte d'arachide, relevée de tomate concentrée et piment, servie avec du riz.
instructions: Dans une grande casserole, fais chauffer 1 c. à soupe d'huile à feu moyen.

Coupe les 2 cuisses de poulet en morceaux de taille moyenne, ajoute-les dans la casserole, fais dorer 5 minutes, en remuant, jusqu'à ce que la surface soit légèrement colorée.

Dans un petit bol, délaye la pâte d'arachide avec 3 c. à soupe d'eau chaude jusqu'à obtenir une consistance lisse.

recipe.title: Garlic Ginger Chicken Stir‑Fry with Broccoli and Rice
recipe.description: A quick, light Asian‑inspired stir‑fry using chicken thighs, broccoli, ginger and garlic, served over fluffy rice.
instructions: Rinse 200 g of rice under cold water, then place in a pot with 300 ml water; bring to a boil over medium heat, then reduce to low, cover and simmer 12 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
While rice cooks, cut the chicken thighs into bite‑size pieces.
Trim the broccoli, cut into florets.
Peel and finely mince the 3 garlic cloves; grate the ginger to make 1 tbsp.

Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok over medium‑high heat; add the chicken and stir‑fry 5 minutes, until the pieces are golden and the internal temperature reaches 74 °C (juices run clear), then remove and set aside.
In the same wok, add the garlic and ginger; stir‑fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the broccoli florets, stir‑fry 3 minutes on medium‑high heat, until bright green and just tender.
Return the chicken to the wok, pour in 2 tbsp soy sauce, add a pinch of salt and pepper; stir‑fry 2 minutes until everything is coated and the sauce thickens slightly.
Slice the spring onion stalks thinly.
Fluff the cooked rice with a fork, divide onto plates, top with the chicken‑broccoli stir‑fry, and garnish with the sliced spring onions.
Serve immediately.
tips: If you prefer a slightly sweeter sauce, add a drizzle of honey or a splash of rice vinegar.
Use the whole chicken thigh, including skin, for extra flavor; trim excess fat before cooking.

recipe.title: Baked Garlic‑Ginger Chicken Thighs with Roasted Broccoli
recipe.description: Oven‑baked chicken thighs marinated in soy‑ginger‑garlic sauce, paired with crispy roasted broccoli – a simple, low‑fat dinner.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels; place in a bowl.
Peel and finely mince the 4 garlic cloves; grate the ginger to make 1 tbsp.
Add 3 tbsp soy sauce, the minced garlic, grated ginger, 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch pepper to the chicken; toss to coat and let marinate while the oven heats (about 5 minutes).
Trim the broccoli and cut into florets; spread on a baking sheet, drizzle with 1 tbsp oil, and season with a pinch of salt and pepper; toss to coat.
Arrange the marinated chicken thighs skin‑side up on the same baking sheet, leaving space between pieces.
Bake for 20 minutes, then flip the chicken and continue baking 5 minutes, until the thickest part of each thigh reaches 74 °C (juices run clear) and the skin is golden and crisp.
Remove from oven; let rest 3 minutes before serving.
Plate the roasted broccoli alongside the baked chicken thighs, spoon any pan juices over the top.
tips: For extra caramelisation, broil for the last 2 minutes, watching closely.
If the thighs are large, cut them in half lengthwise to ensure even cooking within the time limit.

recipe.title: Japanese‑Style Chicken & Egg Rice Soup (Tamagoto)
recipe.description: A comforting, light soup that combines shredded chicken, rice, and silky egg ribbons, flavored with ginger, garlic and soy sauce – perfect for a quick dinner.
instructions: Rinse the 120 g rice under cold water until water runs clear.
Dice the 250 g chicken thighs into small bite‑size pieces.
Peel and mince the 2 garlic cloves; grate the ginger to make 1 tsp.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a medium pot over medium heat; add the garlic and ginger, sauté 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add the chicken pieces, stir‑fry 4 minutes, until no longer pink and the internal temperature reaches 74 °C (juices run clear).
Pour in 800 ml water, bring to a boil over medium‑high heat, then add the rinsed rice.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 12 minutes until the rice is tender and the broth is slightly thickened.
While the soup simmers, beat the 2 eggs in a small bowl.
When the rice is done, increase heat to medium, stir in 1.5 tbsp soy sauce, a pinch of salt and pepper, and gently stream the beaten eggs into the pot while stirring slowly to create thin ribbons.
Cook the egg ribbons for 1 minute, just until set.
Slice the spring onion stalks thinly.
Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with the sliced spring onions, and serve hot.
tips: For a richer broth, add a splash of chicken stock or a dash of mirin.
If you prefer a clearer soup, strain the broth after cooking the chicken and before adding rice.

recipe.title: Tacos de frijol negro con guacamole y salsa fresca
recipe.description: Tacos vegetarianos llenos de frijoles negros, maíz, tomate y un cremoso guacamole de aguacate, perfectos para un almuerzo rápido y nutritivo.
instructions: Escurre y enjuaga 1 lata de frijoles negros y 1 lata de maíz.
Pica finamente 1/2 cebolla morada y 2 tomates en cubos pequeños.
En una sartén a fuego medio, calienta los frijoles y el maíz 3 minutos, revolviendo, hasta que estén tibios.
Añade la cebolla y el tomate picado, cocina 2 minutos más, hasta que la cebolla se vuelva translúcida.
Sazona con 1 pizca de sal y 1 pizca de pimienta.

Mientras se cocinan, prepara el guacamole: corta los 2 aguacates a la mitad, retira el hueso y saca la pulpa con una cuchara. Machaca en un bol, agrega el jugo de 1 lima, una pizca de sal y mezcla hasta obtener una consistencia cremosa.
Calienta las tortillas de maíz en una sartén sin aceite, 30 segundos por lado, hasta que estén flexibles y ligeramente doradas.

Para servir, coloca una cucharada de la mezcla de frijoles y maíz sobre cada tortilla, agrega una porción de guacamole, espolvorea 100 g de queso fresco desmenuzado y termina con un chorrito de jugo de la otra mitad de lima.
tips: Puedes añadir cilantro picado si lo tienes a mano para más frescura.
Si prefieres más picante, agrega unas gotas de salsa picante al guacamole.

recipe.description: Un plato único al estilo latino que combina arroz esponjoso, huevo frito, rodajas de aguacate y una salsa de tomate horneada, listo en menos de 40 minutos.
instructions: Lava el arroz bajo agua corriente hasta que el agua salga clara.
En una olla, combina 200 g de arroz con 400 ml de agua y 1 pizca de sal. Lleva a ebullición, reduce a fuego bajo, tapa y cocina 15 minutos, hasta que el agua se absorba y el arroz esté tierno.
Mientras el arroz se cocina, precalienta el horno a 200 °C.
Corta 2 tomates en cubos y pica finamente 1/4 de cebolla morada.
En una bandeja para horno, mezcla los tomates, la cebolla, 1 cucharada de aceite vegetal, una pizca de sal y pimienta. Hornea 12 minutos, hasta que los tomates se ablanden y empiecen a caramelizar.
En una sartén a fuego medio, agrega un chorrito de aceite y fríe los 2 huevos, 2 minutos por lado para que la yema quede líquida (cocción a fuego medio, borde dorado).
Corta 1 aguacate en rodajas finas y exprime el jugo de 1 lima sobre ellas para evitar que se oxiden.
Para montar el plato, sirve el arroz caliente en dos platos, coloca encima la salsa de tomate horneada, una rodaja de aguacate y el huevo frito. Añade una pizca extra de sal y pimienta al gusto.

Puedes sustituir el aceite vegetal por mantequilla para un sabor más rico.

recipe.description: A hearty one‑pan oven‑cooked stew featuring tender aubergine, chickpeas, and tomatoes, finished with a bright lemon‑tahini sauce and fresh spinach.

Spread the vegetables on a baking tray and roast for 20 minutes on medium heat, until aubergine is golden and tomatoes start to soften.
While the vegetables roast, rinse the canned chickpeas (if using dry, pre‑soak and cook 45 min) and set aside.
In a small saucepan, whisk together the tahini, juice of the lemon, 1 tbsp water, and a pinch of salt to make a smooth drizzle.
After 20 minutes, remove the tray, stir in the chickpeas, and return to the oven for another 10 minutes, until everything is hot and the chickpeas are slightly crisp.
Turn off the oven; stir in the fresh spinach leaves; the residual heat will wilt them in about 2 minutes.
Plate the stew, drizzle the lemon‑tahini sauce over each serving, and serve hot.
tips: For extra smokiness, grill the aubergine cubes on a high heat for 5 minutes before roasting.
If you prefer a thinner sauce, add an extra tablespoon of water to the tahini mixture.

recipe.title: Spicy Chickpea‑Tomato Soup with Spinach and Lemon‑Tahini Swirl
recipe.description: A quick, comforting soup that blends chickpeas, ripe tomatoes, and fresh spinach, finished with a silky lemon‑tahini swirl.
instructions: Dice the tomatoes; mince the garlic; finely chop the onion.

Add the garlic, 1 tsp ground cumin, and 1/2 tsp smoked paprika; stir and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the diced tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to break down.
Pour in 800 ml vegetable broth and bring to a gentle boil over medium‑high heat.
Stir in the drained chickpeas; reduce heat to a low simmer and cook for 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Add the spinach leaves; cook for 2 minutes, just until wilted.
Season with 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch black pepper; taste and adjust if needed.
In a small bowl, whisk together 1 tbsp tahini, the juice of the lemon, and 1 tbsp warm broth from the pot; mix until smooth.
Ladle soup into bowls, swirl a spoonful of the lemon‑tahini mixture into each, and serve hot.
tips: For extra heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper with the spices.
If you prefer a smoother texture, blend half of the soup with an immersion blender before adding spinach.

recipe.title: Pork Tenderloin with Dijon‑Cream Sauce, Leeks and Green Beans
recipe.description: A light yet satisfying oven‑finished pork dish, featuring a silky mustard‑cream sauce, caramelised leeks and crisp green beans.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Trim the pork tenderloin, pat dry, and season with 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large oven‑safe skillet over medium‑high heat; sear the pork on all sides until browned, about 3 minutes per side.
Remove the pork and set aside on a plate.
Thinly slice the leeks (white and light green parts only) and trim the green beans.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the skillet, reduce heat to medium, and sauté the leeks until soft and lightly caramelised, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the Dijon mustard and cream, scraping any browned bits from the pan; bring to a gentle simmer and cook 3 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add the Gruyère, stirring until melted and the sauce is glossy.
Return the pork to the skillet, spoon some sauce over it, and place the skillet in the oven. Roast for 15‑18 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 63°C and the meat is tender.
While the pork finishes, steam the green beans in a pot of boiling water for 5 minutes, then shock in ice water to keep them crisp; drain.
Remove the skillet from the oven, let the pork rest 5 minutes, then slice into medallions.

recipe.title: Leek & Shallot Cream Soup with Gruyère Crumble
recipe.description: Silky French‑style soup made from sweet leeks and shallots, enriched with cream and finished with a crunchy Gruyère topping.
instructions: Trim the leeks, discard dark green tops, and slice the white and light green parts thinly.
Peel and finely dice the shallots.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil and 2 tbsp butter together in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the leeks and shallots, sauté for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are soft and fragrant but not browned.
Season with 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch pepper.
Pour in the stock, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook 12 minutes, until the vegetables are completely tender.
Remove the pot from heat; using an immersion blender, puree the soup until smooth (or blend in batches).
Stir in the cream and return the pot to low heat; warm through for 3 minutes, without boiling.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
For the Gruyère crumble: grate 100 g Gruyère, spread on a small baking sheet, and bake in a pre‑heated 180°C oven for 5‑7 minutes, until golden and crisp. Let cool.
Ladle the soup into bowls and sprinkle each with a generous handful of Gruyère crumble before serving.
tips: For a deeper flavour, add a splash of dry white wine (30 ml) after sautéing the vegetables.
If you like a hint of freshness, finish each bowl with a few drops of cold-pressed olive oil.

recipe.title: Warm Pork & Green‑Bean Salad with Dijon‑Shallot Vinaigrette
recipe.description: A hearty yet light salad that combines sliced pork tenderloin, crisp green beans, and a tangy mustard‑shallot dressing, finished with shaved Gruyère.
instructions: Trim the pork tenderloin, season with ½ pinch salt and ½ pinch pepper, and slice into 1‑cm thick medallions.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium‑high heat; add the pork slices and sear 3 minutes per side until golden and the internal temperature reaches 63°C. Transfer to a plate and let rest.
While the pork rests, trim the green beans and blanch them in boiling salted water for 4 minutes; drain and immediately plunge into ice water to keep them crisp. Pat dry.
Thinly slice the remaining shallot.
Prepare the vinaigrette: in a small bowl whisk together Dijon mustard, apple cider vinegar, 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of pepper until emulsified.
In the same skillet used for the pork, add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat; add the sliced shallot and sauté 2 minutes until soft and fragrant.
Add the blanched green beans to the skillet, toss with the shallot for 2 minutes, then drizzle the vinaigrette over the vegetables and toss to coat.
Slice the rested pork into bite‑size strips and add to the warm salad; toss gently.
Shave the Gruyère with a vegetable peeler over the top of the salad just before serving.
tips: For extra crunch, sprinkle a handful of toasted almond slivers (not in pantry) – optional.
If you prefer a milder vinaigrette, halve the mustard and add a teaspoon of honey.
